newsitem.title: JAPAN: Shokochukin 1.6 pct bond traded at 1.67pct - traders.
newsitem.headline: Shokochukin 1.6 pct bond traded at 1.67pct - traders.

text.p: A 1.6 percent five-year bank debenture issued in December 1996 by Japan's Central Bank for Commercial and Industrial Cooperatives, or Shokochukin Bank, was traded at a yield of 1.67 percent in the secondary market on Friday, bond traders said.
This compares with a yield of 1.65 percent for a similar debenture issued by the Industrial Bank of Japan (IBJ).

"Secondary market yields of Shokochukin and IBJ debentures had been roughly the same until Wednesday. Shokochukin's debenture is now trading about two or three basis points above IBJ's," said a brokerage house trader.
About 1.1 billion yen worth of the December Shokochukin debentures changed hands on Friday, traders said.
Shokochukin debentures came under selling pressure after a senior ruling party official said he was confident that the bank could be privatised.

Koko Sato, head of the Liberal Democratic Party's administrative reform panel, said on Wednesday that the party will present its first proposal for reforming government-backed financial institutions by late April.
